findings.title: Candidate safeguard is suffix-bound, not bound to the exact reserved candidate root
findings.affected_requirement: S3/C64 requires every safeguard source check and test to name the exact reserved candidate root; the candidate gate must never be confused with a candidate or legacy alias.

evidence.detail: The only path check is `$normalizedRoot.EndsWith($reservedTail)`, where `$reservedTail` is the reserved relative suffix. The script then checks only that local repository's branch, cleanliness, and HEAD, not the configured absolute reserved worktree.

findings.reproduction_and_impact: Create or retain another clean repository clone at any path ending in `plans/general-coding-harness/runtime/firmware-v2/worktrees/harness-candidate`, check out branch `firmware/v2-candidate`, include the baseline/configuration, and invoke its copied launcher. It passes the root/branch/clean checks and runs its checks there. An operator could consequently record a green safeguard for that clone rather than the reserved candidate that C4/promotion must certify.
findings.smallest_fix: Resolve the canonical absolute reserved candidate path from the repository's fixed outer-root contract and require case-insensitive equality with `$script:candidateRoot` (while retaining the Git-top-level, branch, clean, and stable-revision checks). Update the safeguard test to reject a same-suffix non-reserved root.
findings.implementation_complexity: Low: replace the suffix predicate with one canonical exact-path comparison and add one focused negative test.
findings.regression_risk: Low: the launcher is intentionally candidate-only and the permitted path is already fixed by the S3 contract.
findings.verification_cost: Low: static inspection plus the focused launcher negative test; no hardware or full safeguard run is required.
findings.cost_benefit_reasoning: The safeguard is the final promotion gate, so accepting a non-reserved clone defeats its candidate-binding purpose. The narrow exact-path check removes that realistic false-credit path with negligible surface area.
